extracted.intended_audience: researchers and teams preparing grant applications to the DoD CDMRP Pancreatic Cancer Research Program (PCARP)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for investigators applying to the Department of Defense Pancreatic Cancer Research Program (PCARP), describing the program's vision, mission, priorities, procedural requirements, and review/consumer involvement mechanisms that will affect proposal evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the burden of pancreatic cancer among Service members, Veterans, their families, and the American public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be framed with the program's overarching vision in mind — work should aim to materially reduce disease burden for the named populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — rigor, innovation, and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote rigorous, innovative, high-impact pancreatic cancer research that leads to prevention, earlier diagnosis, new therapeutic tools, and improved outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation will emphasize scientific rigor, novelty/innovation, and potential for high impact (prevention, early detection, novel therapeutics, improved patient outcomes). Proposals should clearly articulate how they meet these aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on pancreatic cancer-specific needs (detection, diagnosis, therapeutics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pancreatic cancer is aggressive, difficult to detect, has no screening test, is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, and standard treatments have limited effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address these specific challenges (screening/early detection, diagnostic approaches, prevention strategies, and development of new therapeutic tools) rather than general oncology topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit to target populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should benefit Service members, Veterans, their families, and the American public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should describe the relevance and translational potential for these populations and, where appropriate, how study design/population selection reflects these priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding research duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are expected to avoid duplicating existing research efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site links to an 'Avoiding Research Duplication' resource — applicants should demonstrate awareness of existing work and explain how the proposed project is distinct and adds value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-Tiered Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: PCARP uses a two-tiered review process (programmatic/peer review components).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that both scientific/peer-review considerations and programmatic relevance/prioritization will influence funding decisions; align proposals to both scientific merit and program priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: How You are Evaluated (evaluation transparency)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program provides guidance on how applications are evaluated (link: 'How You are Evaluated').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the program's evaluation page for details on review criteria, scoring, and any specific factors reviewers consider when assessing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer involvement and reviewer requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The program incorporates consumer reviewers and provides 'Program Consumer Reviewer Requirements' and 'Consumer Experiences'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and communications should consider lay/consumer perspectives where relevant; understand consumer reviewer roles and any expectations around clear, accessible descriptions of significance and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process requirements (pre-application in eBRAP, eligibility checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Links and resources: 'Start Pre-Application (eBRAP)', 'How To Apply', 'Eligibility Checklist'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow procedural requirements (eBRAP pre-application, eligibility criteria) and should use the provided application instructions and checklists to ensure compliance with submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program strategic priorities and summary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Program provides a Strategic Plan and Summary Sheet (clickable resources) outlining priorities and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the PCARP Strategic Plan and summary materials to align aims, specific aims, and proposed work with stated program priorities and funding focus areas.
